name: Sara Jacobs
stance: Among the most active House members on AI catastrophic and military-safety guardrails — human control of autonomous weapons, national-lab evaluation of frontier AI for CBRN and deception, and a Pentagon AI incident-reporting program.

statements.text: he’s now eliminating the rules trying to keep them in line.

The Pentagon’s move to bring Grok into its classified systems, while pressuring Anthropic to drop key safeguards, is deeply alarming. Undermining AI safety and civil liberties protections could cause large-scale harm.
We need strict guardrails when the military uses AI, whether it’s in Iran or anywhere else – full stop.
We SHOULD have real federal guardrails on AI (but this is far from it), and in the absence of that, states like CA should be able to keep protecting people’s rights and safety.
Introduced a comprehensive AI governance bill to help federal agencies create AI rules.
Congress has been too slow on AI. My approach protects states’ progress and helps federal agencies hold companies accountable when AI is used to break existing federal laws.
Secured NDAA provisions on accountability for the Pentagon's use of AI but announced she would vote against the bill over the lack of guardrails on the use of the military.
Co-introduced the Human Authority over Autonomous Weapons Act with Reps. Beyer and Barrett, barring AI and autonomous weapons from lethal strikes without meaningful human control.
AI mistakes on the battlefield have the potential to be catastrophic: civilian casualties, friendly fire, unintended escalation, and calculations made on faulty data,

Co-led the ATOMIC Act directing the DOE National Labs to evaluate the most advanced AI systems for nuclear and CBRN risks, deceptive behavior and guardrail-bypass, for developers investing at least $2B over five years.
As AI becomes more powerful, we have a responsibility to identify and guard against new risks before they become real-world threats.
Introduced a bipartisan program (in the FY26 NDAA, with Whitesides and Moran) for Department of Defense AI incident and vulnerability reporting.
That's why we need a department-wide program to catch and fix AI incidents and vulnerabilities before they turn into catastrophes.
We don’t have time to wait. The massive threats posed by AI are here and now, and Congress needs to act.

We’re seeing more warnings about the potentially catastrophic risks of AI from bioweapons to nuclear threats. That’s why I co-led the bipartisan ATOMIC Act with @RepMaloyUtah to prevent AI-related nuclear risks before they become real-world emergencies.
We need to act to ensure AI systems are safe, transparent, and accountable. Trump and Republicans need to get on board.

That’s why Congress needs to enact my Defense AI Reliability and Reporting Act, that was in the House-passed NDAA. It would require prompt reporting of near misses like this and a coordinated process to find and fix the underlying failures.

Whether or not to regulate AI should NOT be up for debate. “Winning” the AI race with China doesn’t just mean achieving AGI first – that doesn’t matter if no one trusts these AI systems enough to adopt them or if they hurt people who use them.
Our goal should be to have the right guardrails that make AI systems transparent, safe, and accountable. Trust and safety are our competitive advantage.

AI safety and diplomacy must be at the top of the agenda when President Trump meets with China’s President Xi Jinping. This no-holds-barred race with China over AI is leaving both our countries and the world more vulnerable. We need consistent, bilateral dialogue.
Donald Trump’s plan on AI is to let these companies “self-police.” That’s a recipe for disaster.

OpenAI just disclosed that rogue agents searched federal government websites in ways beyond what they were asked to do. We need urgent action from Congress to put real safeguards on AI before we lose control of this technology.
We need enforceable rules that make AI systems transparent and safe – and hold these companies accountable. “Self-policing” won’t get us there.
Being first in the AI race won’t matter if no one uses what you build – or if you lose control of the technology. That’s why Congress needs to do its job and act on AI now.

Trust and safety are our competitive advantage in the AI race. But to build systems that people actually want to use and trust, Congress needs to act on the societal, model, deployer, and impact levels.
Published a Newsweek op-ed setting out how Congress should regulate AI, from the frontier model level to deployment and impacts.
We need guardrails on AI, NOW. Competition with China is no excuse for letting AI run rampant
